ref: Kindi reply (Kalema copy), char ~54,966; no page markers
gist_en: Kindi says Muhammad cared only for attractive women to marry and for peoples to raid, and claims he had the potency of forty men.
why_excluded: Sexual-potency claim and raid/killing imagery in the same sentence; Aisha not named. Excluded under the exclusion rule. Its Aisha paragraph (P01) is included.

gist_en: Ibn Hajar notes a chronological difficulty in the hadith of Aisha's marriage at six and consummation at nine, and resolves it by dating the consummation after Medina.
why_excluded: Chronology, not an objection to the marriage. Age is only the hadith (team pack).

gist_en: Ibn Hazm imagines a Malikite follower citing Aisha's marriage at six and consummation at nine to validate a minor's will, and rejects the analogy.
why_excluded: Internal legal analogy about wills, not an outside objection to the marriage. Its "special privilege" point is covered by P05.

gist_en: Ibn Hazm answers an objector who reads "deficient in reason and religion" against Aisha and Fatima; about women's merit, not the marriage or age.
why_excluded: Not about the marriage or Aisha's age. Names Aisha only in a list of virtuous women.

ref: Minhaj fi Sharh Muslim, vol. 9, p. 206 (OpenITI marker), commentary on hadith 1422
gist_en: Nawawi says the hadith is explicit proof that a father may marry off a minor daughter without her permission, and surveys the schools.
why_excluded: Legal commentary on the age hadith (duplicate of the team pack); no objection recorded in the windows scanned.

ref: Ikmal al-Muʿlim (Qadi Iyad), vol. 4, p. 572–574 (OpenITI marker), commentary on Muslim hadith 1422
gist_en: Qadi Iyad's commentary on the Aisha marriage hadiths discusses guardianship and the schools; no outside objection is recorded.
why_excluded: Duplicate of the team hadith pack and legal; no objection found in the windows scanned.

ref: Hashimi letter (Muslim side), Kalema copy, char ~24,369
gist_en: The Muslim letter tells Kindi that he may marry up to four wives, divorce, and take concubines, as part of the rules of Islam.
why_excluded: A legal instruction in the Muslim letter, not a reply to an objection. Included here only because the team asked for the wives topic.

ref: Tathbit dala'il al-nubuwwa, vol. 2, p. 528 (OpenITI marker)
gist_en: Abd al-Jabbar says the Prophet had many co-wives, but that no one, including wives, reproached him in anything.
why_excluded: Neutral statement; no objection recorded. Recorded as a negative (the wives are mentioned, no critic).
